overview.title: About NEXUS CHRONICLES
paragraphs: NEXUS CHRONICLES is an interactive web platform developed around NASA’s InSight Mars lander for the Forgotten Equipment challenge.
We built an immersive Mars exploration experience that allows users to navigate mission locations, discover InSight’s story, and explore its scientific instruments and engineering systems.

The platform includes an interactive Investigation section where users examine real mission evidence and scientific visuals, a Go Deeper mode that presents InSight’s scientific findings and data in an accessible way, and an Interactive Engineering Game where users build and develop a space station through progressive levels, applying engineering concepts through hands-on challenges.

Using authentic NASA mission resources and scientific data, NEXUS CHRONICLES turns an abandoned spacecraft into an opportunity to explore real engineering decisions, understand mission challenges, and apply problem-solving skills to future space exploration.

questions.question: Is Mars's core like Earth's?
questions.answer: Earth's outer core is liquid and its inner core is solid. NASA said scientists would keep checking InSight's data to see whether Mars is similar.

secondarySection.title: The machine was more than its parts
paragraphs: how its panels collected energy, how its arm placed delicate instruments, how SEIS listened, and how engineers used radio signals to investigate what they couldn't see.
wasn't successful because every part worked as planned. Some instruments achieved remarkable science. Others faced problems engineers couldn't overcome. Both outcomes taught us something.

optionalGame.title: Mars: The Survival Protocol

moon.name: The Moon
moon.description: Humanity's primary stepping stone into the cosmos. NASA's Apollo missions left behind landing stages, rovers, and scientific packages that continue yielding discoveries.

equipment.name: Apollo 11 Lunar Module Descent Stage ("Eagle")
equipment.summary: The lower half and landing gear of the Eagle Lunar Module, used by Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin. Serves as the landing base and holds the commemorative stainless-steel plaque.
keyFacts: First crewed spacecraft landing base on another celestial body
Carries the commemorative plaque: "Here men from the planet Earth first set foot upon the Moon. We came in peace for all mankind."
Equipped with Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP) sub-assemblies

equipment.name: Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector (LRRR)
equipment.site: Tranquility Base & Fra Mauro & Hadley Rille
equipment.summary: Precision corner-cube prism arrays that bounce Earth-fired laser pulses back to terrestrial telescopes with picosecond time-of-flight resolution.
keyFacts: The only Apollo experiment that continues to collect scientific telemetry today
Measures the Earth-Moon distance down to a few millimeters
Proven that the Moon is slowly spiraling away from Earth at 3.8 cm per year

equipment.name: Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV - "Moon Buggy")
equipment.summary: Electric four-wheel rover engineered by Boeing and Delco. Allowed astronauts to venture up to 35 kilometers away from the lunar module, carrying geologic drill cores and rock samples.
keyFacts: Capable of 13 km/h speed across jagged regolith slopes
Left permanently parked with high-gain directional antenna aimed at Earth
Apollo 17 rover drove a total record distance of 35.9 km across lunar valleys

equipment.name: Passive Seismic Experiment Package (PSEP)
equipment.summary: High-sensitivity long-period seismometers powered by radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs) to map the Moon's deep crustal stratification and core.
keyFacts: Detected over 12,000 seismic events, including deep tidal moonquakes and meteor impacts
Revealed that the Moon has a crust ~60 km thick and a small metallic core

mars.name: The Mars
mars.description: A rust-colored desert world shaped by ancient rivers, towering volcanoes, and violent dust storms. NASA robotic scouts have traversed hundreds of kilometers across Martian sands.

equipment.name: Perseverance Mars Rover
equipment.summary: NASA’s most sophisticated planetary explorer, seeking biosignatures of ancient microbial life in a dried river delta lakebed and caching core samples for future retrieval to Earth.
keyFacts: Carries MOXIE: First technology demonstration converting Martian CO₂ into breathable oxygen
Equipped with 23 advanced cameras, SuperCam Raman laser, and PIXL x-ray fluorescence
Cached over 25 pristine hermetic geological core samples for Mars Sample Return

equipment.name: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter ("Ginny")
equipment.summary: The historic first rotorcraft in human civilization to achieve controlled, powered flight on another planet, overcoming Mars’s ultra-thin atmosphere (less than 1% of Earth’s density).
keyFacts: Designed for 5 test flights; completed 72 flights spanning 17 kilometers
Dual counter-rotating carbon-fiber blades spinning at 2,400+ RPM
Served as an aerial scout finding traversable pathways for the Perseverance rover

equipment.name: Curiosity Rover (Mars Science Laboratory)
equipment.summary: The 1-ton rover that determined ancient Mars had freshwater lakes, neutral pH, and all chemical ingredients required to sustain microbial life billions of years ago.
keyFacts: Climbing Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons), inspecting millions of years of layered Martian strata
Onboard Sample Analysis at Mars (SAM) laboratory detects organic carbon molecules
Has driven over 31 kilometers and beamed back hundreds of thousands of raw images

equipment.name: InSight Lander
equipment.summary: NASA's planetary crust observatory that listened to the heartbeat of Mars, placing the ultra-sensitive SEIS seismometer under a vacuum wind-shield dome.
keyFacts: Recorded over 1,319 marsquakes, revealing an active, tremor-filled interior
Measured Mars's liquid iron-nickel core with a radius of approximately 1,830 kilometers

equipment.name: Viking 1 & 2 Descent Landers
equipment.summary: Humanity's first successful long-duration surface stations on Mars, transmitting the first high-resolution color surface panoramas and atmospheric weather reports.
keyFacts: Operated for over 6 years on the Martian surface (Viking 1 ceased 1982)
Performed biological pyrolytic release and gas exchange soil experiments
